items.title: 52263_Sonny Greer oral history interview
items.q: I say, 'Hey, Miss Bruskey, I can beat that guy drumming you got in that band. He ain't nothing.' I say, 'I can't beat him.' Now, I'm her star pupil in German language.

ctx.x: laying off for a week, didn't have to go back to New York, so I invited him to my house, I said, 'Come on, you just well stay down here at the seashore for a week, and rest and have fun, go bathing, swimming, have some fun.' He said, 'You mean that,' and I said yeah, and my mother was tickled to death. She didn't know I was playing -- learning how to play no drums. My mother loved to cook, my sisters experts, and we'd fatten this turkey up, and I'm still taking them lessons.

Now, after he left and went to New York after he stayed a week with us as our guest, I went to school and I run into my German teacher. I say, 'Hey, Miss Bruskey, I can beat that guy drumming you got in that band. He ain't nothing.' I say, 'I can't beat him.' Now, I'm her star pupil in German language. She said, 'oh, you're kidding.' Said, 'no, I'm serious.' She said, 'I tell you what you do, you give me an audition.'

I said, 'All you got to do is bring the piano player,' had a good white boy, you know, hell of a piano player, so he come down and in the meantime they had an eight-piece band that played all the basketball games, all the affairs around that school, so she come around -- I dropped this thing on her. I went through the whole repertoire, man, like Peggie just showed me. Her mouth flew open, never closed. She said 'You sing.' I say, 'do I sing. Does a mockingbird,' so I could sing.
